text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000064 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation, with nearly half of those claims on patients with few or no chronic conditions, but the records returned are too thin to confirm or refute the billing pattern.","leaning":"pattern_consistent_with_upcoding","interpretation":"The excess 99215 share holds after risk adjustment and appears in every complexity stratum, including patients with zero or one condition. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims carry simple diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection (C0031862, C0031885), rash (C0031824), low back pain (C0031936) and follow-up codes (C0031929, C0031931), which is the more concerning part of the pattern than a sicker panel would explain. The documentation cannot settle this: only one 99215 claim has records, and it is C0031775, a four-condition patient whose note supports high MDM, so it says nothing about the low-complexity claims. The lower levels look largely supported, with one 99214 documented below billed (C0031854) and one moderate-plus data-reviewed note lacking a lab line, which is weak evidence at most. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed above and check whether their MDM and time support level 5, and watch for cloned or templated notes."}
